events.title: Adult Book Discussion: Theft
events.description: In November, the Cupertino Library Adult Book Discussion Group will talk about the 2025 novel Theft by Nobel Prize-winning author Abdulrazak Gurnah. Karim and Badar are two young men living on the East African island of Zanzibar. Karim's mother Raya leaves her abusive older husband when Karim is three, taking her son with her. However, when she finds a happy marriage with her new husband Haji Othman, Raya allows her parents to raise her son instead. Years later, when Karim is a university student living with his mother and stepfather for convenience, he meets and befriends the orphaned teenaged boy Badar, whose neglectful relatives force him to become a domestic servant in Haji Othmann's household. There, Badar is treated as a servant, although he is actually Othman's nephew. Fauzia, Karim's beautiful, studious girlfriend, teaches Badar the cooking and housekeeping skills he needs to become a successful domestic servant. Badar's fragile new security is abruptly destroyed when he is accused of theft and dismissed. Even though Karim helps him get a new job at a local hotel, things are never the same between them. The Adult Book Discussion Group meets twice a month, on the third Thursday morning at 11 am and on the third Thursday evening at 7 PM. Meetings are held in Room 201B. All meetings are sponsored by The Friends of the Cupertino Library. For accessibility accommodations (e.g., ASL), please fill out the online form at sccld.org/accessibility 7+ days prior to the event. If you need assistance with the form, speak with a staff member at your local library, call (408) 540-3945, or email us at ask@sccl.org.

stanfordSources.title: SVRMP Relaunch Mentorship Kickoff Event
stanfordSources.description:
Purpose of the Event

  • Formally announce mentor-mentee pairings
  • Establish expectations and program norms
  • Build immediate community and rapport

What to Expect:

We want to keep the evening structured but highly social. Our 60-minute agenda include:

  • Welcome & Program Overview: A brief walk-through of the timeline, monthly expectations, and support resources.
  • The Big Reveal: We will be doing a physical envelope reveal alongside a slideshow on the TV to formally announce each mentor-mentee pairing!
  • Breakout Time: You will have 10–15 minutes to sit down with your partner, grab food, and find a few shared goals.
  • Next Steps & Gift Cards: We’ll outline our accountability milestones—including the gift cards distribution for your initial 1:1 meeting!

Event Details:

Date: Thursday, 29 October 2026

Time: 1800

Location: OMAC, Old Union 2nd Floor, Room 218

scuSource.title: GBP & MSSB Fireside Chat: SF Giants
scuSource.description:
Graduate Business Career Services, in partnership with the MS Sports Business program, is pleased to host our next esteemed guest, Lan Huynh Lee - VP, People & Culture at the SF Giants, as part of the program’s “Luminary Speaker Series”.

Join us on 11/05 for a Fireside Chat with Lan on “Breaking into the Sports Industry”. With a successful career track record including more than 15 years with the Giants, and earlier experience working in media and HR consulting, Lan will share career advice, industry insights, and anecdotes as part of an overall discussion focused on:
  • practical advice for breaking into the sports industry
  • building and sustaining a professional network
  • guidance for standing out in the hiring process
  • identifying career growth opportunities.
Event Details:
  • 5th November 2026
  • 4:30 PM - 5:30 PM
  • Lucas Hall 209 
  • This is an in-person event only. 
Registration is required - please Register Here for the SF Giants Fireside Chat.
